about: This file lists every kind of building block that a tweak or a book record can be made of, from the design in docs/overrides-redesign.md (Building blocks, item 1). scripts/blocks-check.mjs reads it: every row needs a status, a 'ruled' row names the ruling that fixes how it shows, and a row that is 'built' means the block registry src/rules/blocks/registry.ts has an entry with this id (REGISTERED: the entry's 'applies' field says whether the block already reaches the character, and the check prints the ones that do not). For a built row, bookFields lists the stored record fields its book blocks are read from, the same list as its registry entry (the check compares them); for any other row, the fields that hold that kind of rule today.

rows.title: Bonus or penalty
rows.note: Adds a number to a stat (not attribute scores, see attribute.add); a tweak always adds unless the player picks a PF2e bonus type, and a book bonus keeps its type.

rows.title: Set a number
rows.note: Replaces the permanent total of a stat, and conditions and modes still apply on top of it.

rows.title: Set a number: at least N
rows.note: Lifts a stat to N when it is lower and does nothing when it is already N or more (the same floor shape as Land Legs).

rows.title: Set maximum HP
rows.note: Wraps the old overrides.maxHp key. Part B WP3 (case C): a 'set' term of the max-HP list, so a mode's max HP bonus, a Con mode and Drained count on top of it.

rows.title: Raise or lower an attribute score
rows.note: Stored in overrides.blocks; a +/- on an attribute changes the score itself, so every reader of the score agrees (spec item 8).

rows.title: Set an attribute score
rows.note: Wraps the old overrides.attributes key.

rows.title: Rank: at least (also Add a Lore)
rows.note: Wraps overrides.proficiencies (meta mode 'atLeast'). Part A seeds it as a floor, so later skill increases and class raises still go up from it; a Lore with any subject keys through loreKey.

rows.title: Rank: exactly
rows.note: Wraps overrides.proficiencies (meta mode 'exactly'). Part A adds the final clamp after every raise, so a rank the player lowered stays lowered.

rows.title: Old rank, kept as it was
rows.note: An old overrides.proficiencies entry with no 'at least' or 'exactly' recorded. It keeps today's behaviour until part B sorts it into one of the two at read time; never offered as a new tweak.

rows.title: Give a feat
rows.note: Wraps overrides.addedFeats, at any level. Part A makes a given feat work exactly like the same feat picked in a slot (fix case D).

rows.title: Add a language
rows.note: Wraps the old overrides.addedLanguages key.

rows.title: Add a spell
rows.note: Wraps overrides.addedSpells (an innate spell or a ritual); other ways to cast a given spell are grant.spellYourWay in phase 3.

rows.title: Give a class feature
rows.note: Wraps overrides.addedFeatures as a list entry only; making it work like a picked class feature (its bonuses, uses and choices) is phase 3.

rows.title: Remove a feat the build gave
rows.note: Wraps overrides.removedFeatIds; removing what that feat gave is remove.withWhatItGave in phase 3.

rows.title: Take anyway in a picker
rows.note: Wraps overrides.allowedFeats (feats only); a rule-breaking pick gets a small warning mark and is never refused. Every other picker is choice.allowAnywayAnyPicker.

rows.title: Take anyway in every other picker
rows.note: Registered by Tweaks phase 2 WP1; built in WP4 (applies: blocks): the heritage, background, deity, both subclass pickers, sanctification, and the spell pickers (each class pool, the second class, a dedication's book ranks and archetype pool, open spell choices picked or granted). Two engine seams read it: the open spell grant's tradition rule and a dedication's named cantrips. A skill increase's cap / locked / narrowed rules (WP12) come after the record rebuild (WP13: no picker offers them; a stored one reads as made in a newer version). Still open: the archetype rules, pick-a-feat prerequisites (C41), option prerequisites inside a choice, Path to Perfection.

rows.title: Change a feat's or class feature's name or text
rows.note: Wraps overrides.contentEdits. Part A sends it through one content path, so it reaches the party card and the tracker too; showing the new text and name on the card is phase 4.

rows.title: Set one part, the rest keeps counting
rows.note: Sets one input of a stat, such as HP per level, so the total still follows level-up.

rows.title: Grows with level
rows.note: A value that grows: +1 more at chosen levels, half your level, or per feat held (the Resiliency shape, which must shrink again when feats are removed).

rows.title: A named statistic with no row (impulse attack, scroll DC)
rows.ruling: gold-set Round 9 'Special statistic' and Q30; mechanic-lanes specialStatistic test
rows.note: Shown on the Special statistics card with its own breakdown, only when the text names the statistic and no other row already prints that number.

rows.title: Battle form: replace your stats
rows.ruling: gold-set Q3 and Round 10 (noStrikes, size, temporary HP)
rows.note: A mode that really replaces the stats it names and says plainly that it is on; a stat it does not name stays the character's own, and tweak +/- do not apply during it.

rows.title: Rank goes up at a later level
rows.note: "At 7th level you become master in it": one or more later steps on a rank the same record gave.

rows.title: Rank in one weapon or weapon group
rows.note: "Trained in longbows" or "expert with swords", using the same at least / exactly rules as rank.atLeast.

rows.title: Rank of a spellcasting entry
rows.note: Spell attack and spell DC rank for one casting entry, applied after the entry is retuned, and it keeps rising with the class.

rows.title: Use one skill in place of another
rows.note: The swap applies only when it makes the player better, never lowering a number.

rows.title: If already trained, pick another skill
rows.note: A book rule that turns a wasted training into a different skill or a higher rank. book-only: waits for the re-implementation (decision 25); not a phase-2 tweak.

rows.title: Class DC of another class (archetype)
rows.note: A dedication's class DC for a class you do not have, shown on the Multiclass DCs card; phase 6 reuses it for each extra class's own class DC.

rows.title: Fixed attribute boost or flaw
rows.note: A boost or flaw that follows the PF2e boost rules, unlike attribute.add which moves the score directly; an extra boost a tweak adds is choice.addPlace. book-only: waits for the re-implementation (decision 25); not a phase-2 tweak.

rows.title: Apex: raise to 18, or by 2
rows.note: Raises an attribute to 18, or by 2 if it is already 18 or more. book-only: waits for the re-implementation (decision 25); not a phase-2 tweak.

rows.title: Use a different attribute for a stat
rows.note: "I Intimidate with Strength": the stat keeps following that attribute (feature 50). No ruling limits a player's own choice; gold-set Q10's betterRank is about rank remaps in book feats.

rows.title: Give a spell your way (at will, per day, slots, focus)
rows.note: Chooses how a given spell is cast: at will, X times per day, from your slots, or as a focus spell.

rows.title: A record grants a class feature with its choice
rows.note: A granted class feature shows its details and offers its own choice, the shape grant.classFeature must reach in phase 3.

rows.title: Give an action, reaction or activity
rows.ruling: gold-set principles E and H, Q4
rows.note: A reaction appears in the reactions list with trigger and requirements in its popup, and an action whose cost changes is listed under both costs.

rows.title: Give an ancestry feature or heritage
rows.note: Gives an ancestry feature or a second heritage that really works, like a picked one.

rows.title: Give an item
rows.note: Gives the character an item from the rules, stored on the character so it travels to the GM.

rows.title: Add a creature trait (undead, aquatic...)
rows.note: Recorded on the Details tab; a trait true only while a form runs lives on that form's mode.

rows.title: Change what another record gave
rows.note: A feat that changes another record's grant is shown inside that granted thing.

rows.title: Create a new thing for this character only
rows.note: A new feat, action, item, spell, class feature, heritage, ancestry, deity, language or choice list, made of blocks and stored inside the character.

rows.title: Pick from any list
rows.note: Built in Tweaks phase 2 WP5 (applies: blocks): a general feat in a class slot, another ancestry's feat, a feat above your level or past its only level, in the feat slots, the pick-a-feat pickers and the three bonus feat pickers (Versatile Human, Unified Magical Theory, a dedication's bonus skill feat); open feat choices wait. Mythic and impulse slot rules are not liftable. Taking the same feat more times is choice.moreTakes.

rows.title: Take a feat more times
rows.note: Decision 17 (C2): the same feat more times than it allows, its own kind. Built in Tweaks phase 2 WP8 (applies: blocks): one tweak per feat raises the take cap of the feat slots and extra places (the slot and place pickers' Take again, the Tweaks page's Add); a second copy adds only what can add up: its own slot-keyed answer counts (Canny Acumen's save, Different Worlds' Lore, Natural Ambition's feat), but a once-only feat's answers keyed by the feat id are shared, so a second copy adds no answer of its own there: its spell choice (Minor Deific Power, Minor Magic, Spell Runes), skill choice (Natural Skill), cantrip choice (Arcane Tattoos), bonus skill feat (Magical Knowledge) and other choices (Magical Resistance's energy type); the row says which. A feat more times through a feat's own pick (pick-a-feat grants) and auto-granted feats keep the book's cap. The daily items lane keeps the book's count of takings too: a once-only feat with daily temporary items (Gadget Specialist, Basic Scroll Cache, Herbal Forager) taken more times still prepares one taking's items (dailyItems.ts).

rows.title: Add a choice place (extra feat slot, boost...)
rows.note: Built in Tweaks phase 2 WP7 (applies: blocks) for the extra feat place: the level page's Add a place and its place card, and the Tweaks page's Add a place; WP11 built the extra skill increase (its own lane after the level's main, bonus and background increases, with the level's cap) and the extra attribute boost (its own breakdown line), each a carrier holding its answer, with their level-page cards and the Tweaks page's place kind and answer part. Phase 2: feat place, skill increase, boost; an extra class-feature choice waits (WP15's one reader is its first half); cantrip and spell known come with spellcasting.cantrip / spellcasting.slot (phase 5). Book feat slots live in the FEAT_PICK_GRANTS code table today.

rows.title: Answer a choice outside its list
rows.note: Registered by Tweaks phase 2 WP1 (applies: not-yet); WP10 delivers it after the record rebuild. Until then (WP13) a stored one reads as made in a newer version: kept byte for byte, shown read-only, never applied, and the write door refuses a new one. Pick a skill a feat's list does not offer; today the resolvers drop such answers silently. The answer families reached and the ones waiting are section 4b of the phase-2 plan.

rows.title: Add or remove options in a choice list
rows.note: Registered by Tweaks phase 2 WP1 (applies: not-yet); WP9 delivers it after the record rebuild. Until then (WP13) a stored one reads as made in a newer version: kept byte for byte, shown read-only, never applied, and the write door refuses a new one. Example: add fire to the energy types a feat offers. C38: no book field moves; book analog: choiceOptionAdditions / choiceOptionLimits, moved in the big job.

rows.title: A choice the book asks (choose one of these)
rows.ruling: gold-set R13, R14, principles I and K, Q20, Q26
rows.note: "Either X or Y" is one control, free text is a valid answer, a value the book works out from the character gets no picker, and an answer must reach something.

rows.title: An option that itself grants something
rows.note: The answer to a choice decides what is granted, falling back to the default grant when unanswered so no saved character loses it. book-only: waits for the re-implementation (decision 25); not a phase-2 tweak.

rows.title: Chosen at daily preparations
rows.note: Asked when the player presses Daily preparations, never in the builder, and defaults to the last answer; a daily rank never counts as a build rank.

rows.title: Give spellcasting
rows.note: A whole, separate casting entry (prepared or spontaneous, tradition, key attribute, slot table), as feature 21 asks.

rows.title: Change spellcasting (tradition, key attribute...)
rows.note: Changes an entry's tradition, prepared or spontaneous, or key attribute, including a book retune limited to spells from certain sources.

rows.title: Extra spell slot
rows.note: Adds (or removes) slots of a rank on one casting entry.

rows.title: Learn a cantrip
rows.note: Adds a cantrip to an entry; under Dual Class only the class it was taken for gets it (book cantrips also sit in the FEAT_CANTRIP_GRANTS code table).

rows.title: Add spells to a spell list or curriculum
rows.note: Widens what an entry may prepare or learn, such as a wizard school's curriculum.

rows.title: Domain access
rows.note: A deity's or a feat's domains, which decide the domain spells offered.

rows.title: Tradition of a granted spell
rows.note: The tradition the text names is stored per spell, and one the book works out from the character is derived, never asked.

rows.title: Granted spell depends on the character
rows.note: "If you have void healing, you instead cast harm": the app works it out and shows no picker.

rows.title: Granted spell heightens with a skill or level
rows.ruling: gold-set R7 (a floor, the Land Legs shape)
rows.note: A heighten step is a floor, never a replacement that could lower a spell the character already casts higher.

rows.title: Remove anything (feature, spell, language, sense...)
rows.note: Removes a class, ancestry or heritage feature, a spell, a language, a proficiency or a sense; removing a weakness is the one precedent today.

rows.title: Remove: only this, or this and what it gave
rows.ruling: gold-set R11 (things given when added disappear when removed); design decision 7
rows.note: Asks each time; it can point at each granted block because every block carries its source id and a fixed key.

rows.title: Switch off one bonus or star from something you keep
rows.note: Keep the feat but turn off its +1 AC or a wrong star, pointing at the book block's fixed key.

rows.title: Remove a choice place
rows.note: Built in Tweaks phase 2 WP6 for printed feat slots and WP14 for skill increase and boost places. Class-feature-choice places (WP16), a commander's tactic places and a runesmith's rune places (WP17) come after the record rebuild (WP13: no picker offers them; a stored one reads as made in a newer version). Not removable: an ancestry's or background's fixed boost, a class's key boost, a second class's key boost, the kineticist's element group, a class's initial trained skills. Removing class features, ancestry or heritage features, spells, languages, proficiencies and senses is feature 17 (phase 3); removing spellcasting is feature 22 (phase 5); removing a list's options is feature 15 (choice.editOptions); spell places wait for phase 5, places a record gives and bonus language places for phase 3; formula picks are not places; a place a feat adds to a count (Additional Ikon, Tactical Expansion, Tactical Excellence) is phase 3. Anything already picked in a removed place stays as a feat with no slot and is never lost silently.

rows.title: Remove spellcasting
rows.note: A class without its spells, or one casting entry removed; no such mechanism exists today.

rows.title: Change the description of any record
rows.note: Spells, items, actions, ancestries, conditions too; the card shows your text with a Show original switch.

rows.title: Rename or reskin
rows.note: The new name shows everywhere, with the book name small underneath.

rows.title: Change properties (traits, action cost, range...)
rows.note: Traits, action cost, level, frequency, range, area, duration, damage, Bulk, price; the editor says plainly when an effect is built into the app's code and cannot change.

rows.title: Effect on an ally: a mark on your own record
rows.ruling: mechanic-lanes Ruling F + N; gold-set principle A
rows.note: No number on your sheet for a bonus that lands on someone else, but the record it modifies (a spell, an action) carries a visible mark.

rows.title: Mark on the record a feat widens
rows.ruling: gold-set principle C and Q8; mechanic-lanes Ruling G
rows.note: The mark lives on the class feature, action or condition the player looks at (RECORD_MARKERS code table today).

rows.title: Bonus with no stat row marks the action or condition
rows.ruling: mechanic-lanes Ruling D (including its DC-only rule)
rows.note: The value sits inline on the action or condition with a star to its source; a save DC gets a breakdown entry and a skill DC gets nothing.

rows.title: Running effect shown as a display-only mode
rows.ruling: mechanic-lanes Ruling E and Ruling F; gold-set Q1, Q15, principle B
rows.note: An effect lasting longer than a round, or a complicated critical-success effect, shows as a mode carrying its full text; HP and damage never move sheet stats.

rows.title: Note-only change (a star on a stat)
rows.ruling: mechanic-lanes Rulings A, B, C, G, H, I and Stacking as displayed; gold-set principles D, J, Q20, R1, R2, desk #163 and #177
rows.note: "+2 vs poison" as a star on the stat or Strike it affects, with no change to the number; a bonus only inside a feat's own activity stars nothing.

rows.title: Degree of success shifts
rows.note: One entry stars the skill and marks the action (all three saves when it applies to saves), in both directions, better and worse.

rows.title: Add a note to any record
rows.note: Your own text under the book text, without replacing it; books use it for a clause worth printing but not computed.

rows.title: Text a record adds to a spell it grants
rows.note: Written into that spell's description under the granting record's name, set apart from the spell's own rules.

rows.title: Deliberately nothing on the sheet
rows.ruling: gold-set R2, R6, principle P, Q5, Q15, Round 9 (ephemeral, roll twice, fast healing)
rows.note: Marks a clause the owner ruled needs no surface, so an audit knows it was checked rather than missed.

rows.title: Raise a limit (focus points, reactions, invested...)
rows.note: Max focus points, hero points, reactions, the investiture limit, Bulk limit, mythic points, class pools (vials, tactics, runes, scroll slots) and the Dying and Doomed limits.

rows.title: Uses per day (frequency)
rows.note: "Once per day" gets use pips that reset on rest; a once-per-round frequency gets no pip.

rows.title: Starts at a level
rows.note: Every tweak's start level: not a kind of its own (it has no storage and no seam), but the `level` part of each tweak's editor, built in part B (stored in overrides.meta `from`, a given feat's or class feature's own stored level, or a block's `from`; plan B, B18). The book side (`innateSpells.minLevel`, a spell ladder such as "at 10th level you can also cast") waits for the big re-implementation.

rows.title: While a state is on (raging, a stance, panache)
rows.ruling: gold-set Q11, Q1, R3, principle B; design decision 16
rows.note: Something that can be shut down is a mode, otherwise a passive bonus; the shared part needs one list of states (whileActive has 5 values, the others 4).

rows.title: Aura (an emanation around you)
rows.note: A mode with category Aura plus a star carrying the positional condition; nothing is worked out from who stands inside it.

rows.title: Rules on a choice (only at 1st level, different each time)
rows.ruling: gold-set Q9, Q21 and principle Q, Q27
rows.note: Illegal options are hidden unless the player shows them, options that cannot be taken are greyed with a reason, and only a grant wasted for the whole career is filtered.

rows.title: Dedication rule (two feats before another dedication)
rows.note: Only a feat that prints the clause gates, with its own archetypes, count and exception.

rows.title: Enhancement: a benefit you have only when named
rows.note: A second tier printed on a feat that counts only while another record points at it. book-only: waits for the re-implementation (decision 25); not a phase-2 tweak.

rows.title: Add a resistance
rows.note: Resistance N to a damage type, including values worked out from level.

rows.title: Add an immunity
rows.note: Immune to a damage type, condition or effect.

rows.title: Add a weakness
rows.note: Weakness N to a damage type; a top-level weaknesses field on an item is read by nothing.

rows.title: Void healing (harmed by vitality)
rows.note: The undead-style healing switch that some heritages, items and Zombie Dedication give.

rows.title: Add a sense (darkvision, scent...)
rows.note: Darkvision shows alone when it supersedes low-light vision.

rows.title: Add a movement type (fly, swim, climb, burrow)
rows.ruling: gold-set principle F, Q7, Q16, desk #153
rows.note: The speed itself, with a star only when it is conditional, and formulas for speeds that follow your land Speed.

rows.title: Extra damage or a bigger damage die
rows.note: "+1d6 fire" or a die step on one weapon or on all Strikes.

rows.title: Add or remove weapon traits
rows.note: A trait added to Strikes is its own lane; a rider with a printed way to end it lives on a mode.

rows.title: New unarmed attack (claws, horns)
rows.note: Adds a Strike with its own die, traits and range.

rows.title: Critical specialization
rows.note: Gives the critical specialization effect for a weapon, group or unarmed attack.

rows.title: Multiple attack penalty changes
rows.note: A record states its own pair and replaces the default, never subtracting. A player's own MAP change was dropped (dropped idea 4), so this reaches Tweaks only as a book-only part under Advanced (decision 24).

rows.title: Reach
rows.note: Reach is a value on the Strike, several reaches shown together and conditional ones starred; size alone never grants reach.

rows.title: A deity's favoured weapon
rows.note: The weapon a deity names, which other feats then read.

rows.title: A record gives a companion, familiar or eidolon
rows.ruling: mechanic-lanes Companions ruling; gold-set principle M2
rows.note: A companion's bonus and items belong on the companion, not on you; a temporary creature is added by the player (book grants sit in the companionGrants code tables).

rows.title: Tweak a companion, familiar or eidolon
rows.note: Number, defense and strike blocks with a companion as the owner of the target, plus a breakdown popup the companions do not have today.

rows.title: Familiar abilities: locked ones and the budget
rows.note: Locked abilities, whether they count against the limit, and the daily budget, where two raises of the same base take the higher (FEAT_COMPANION_GRANTS code table).

rows.title: Armour stats (AC, Dex cap, check penalty...)
rows.note: Armour numbers on an item, including items stored as something else that are really worn armour (no field exists for that yet).

rows.title: Hardness, Broken Threshold and shield HP
rows.note: A shield's or object's durability numbers.

rows.title: Runes on an item (built-in or copied)
rows.note: Runes printed into an item's own name (no field exists yet) and items that copy another item's runes.

rows.title: Material, disguise and ignored Bulk
rows.note: Plain properties of an item: its precious material, what it appears to be, and Bulk it ignores.

rows.title: Item activation
rows.note: "Activate (2 actions)" and what the activation does.

rows.title: Item charges and uses
rows.note: Charges or uses per day held by an item.

rows.title: Consumable behaviour (potion, scroll, talisman)
rows.note: Instantaneous gets no mode, ongoing with numbers gets a real mode, ongoing without numbers gets a display-only mode.

rows.title: Spell held in an item (staff, wand)
rows.note: An item whose activation casts a spell, keyed by the spell's rank.

rows.title: Formula book entries a feat grants
rows.note: A one-time write into the book's own state, never a live derivation; losing the book loses the formulas.

rows.title: Change your size
rows.note: Sets the character's size; a battle form's size is shown on the Details tab naming the form.

rows.title: More classes
rows.note: A third or fourth class with its level range, switches for what it gives, best-of or added, and its own class DC (decision 5).

rows.title: Change class basics (key attribute, HP per level...)
rows.note: Key attribute, HP per level, starting proficiencies, trained skills and the attribute for class DC.

rows.title: Class archetype replaces class features
rows.ruling: gold-set 2026-10-15 Dual Class rulings (only its own class loses it; Warrior of Legend's cap is the fighter side only)
rows.note: Removes or swaps class features of the one class the archetype belongs to.

rows.title: Change what a class table gives at a level
rows.note: Class table changes held in the CLASS_ADVANCEMENT code table (advancement.ts) today.

notBlocks.why: Parts every tweak shares, not kinds of block: the reason (30), the breakdown line, which is each number block's breakdown wording in the registry (31), the Tweaks list (32) and the on/off switch (33); part B builds them in phase 1.
Tweaks panel features (groups, a rules-only view, copy to another character) that act on many tweaks at once; they go into whichever phase touches the panel.

Behaviour every block has: a block whose book record changed shows a compare view (39), and a block whose record or target is missing shows as broken with Remove and Point to another, never dropped (40, the registry's 'show-broken').
Save as homebrew is an action that copies blocks into a homebrew record (source kind 'homebrew', reserved in phase 1), not a block kind; phase 4.
Dropped: GM marks and list (decision 3), the GM gives tweaks (already possible through the GM edit view and the never-overwrite door), a Change this button on the sheet (decision 2).
Moved out of Tweaks: following a deity with any class is a normal builder fix, done in its own chat (Guy, 2026-10-14).
Dropped idea 7, use the older printing of one record: against gold-set R12 (the newest printing wins, whole). Dropped idea 9: Modes stay a separate system (decision 16).

mechanic-lanes NOT lanes (flavour, GM-adjudicated outcomes, effects on enemies or the battlefield, the internal steps of an activity, restated general rules, prerequisites, access, crafting, price and Bulk lines) are never mechanical, so no block holds them.

Gold-set rulings about process or single records, not about how a kind of effect shows: Q12, Q17, Q18, Q24, R8, R9, R10, R15, R16, desk #164, #171, #173, #175, #176, Adapted Cantrip, the GM-edit answers and the Mauler 'future correctness pass' principle. R17 (the trust gate) is a switch over every book block, not a kind.
